title: Comments and Documentation Comments
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of comments and documentation comments in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply comments and documentation comments in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to comments that explain intent and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Comments and Documentation Comments through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding comments and documentation comments helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Comments and Documentation Comments helps you reason about single-line comments. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Single-line comments. Then connect it to Multi-line documentation conventions. The remaining syllabus points—Comments that explain intent—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports comments and documentation comments. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for comments and documentation comments using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Comments that explain intent), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
